meta.title: Mae Bio Inspirations: Mantis Shrimp Hyperspectral Vision

chunks.title: Mantis Shrimp Vision Biology
chunks.content: Mantis shrimp have 12-16 specialized photoreceptor types vs human 3. Compound eyes with tens of thousands of ommatidia. Four rows handle UV and visible light, two rows specialize in polarized light. Each eye sees depth independently and moves independently. Uses temporal scanning with binning (barcode scanner approach) rather than opponent processing. Prioritizes speed (instant categorization into behavioral categories) over precision (subtle discrimination). Only known animal detecting circularly polarized light - used for species-specific private signaling.

chunks.title: Mantis Shrimp Computational Model
chunks.content: SIMPOL (Stomatopod Inspired Multispectral and POLarization sensitive) sensor: stacked polarization-sensitive layers with polymer retarders. Each layer captures different spectral+polarization combination. 15 spectral channels over 350nm bandwidth with 16.9nm resolution. Snapshot hyperspectral and polarimetric sensing in single pixel. Computational model: N-channel parallel sensing, each with narrow response function. Winner-take-all binning: strongest-responding channel determines category. Minimal cross-channel comparison.

chunks.title: Mantis Shrimp Mae Architecture Mapping
chunks.content: Proposed HyperspectralSensor in new sensing/ module. 16 parallel analysis channels per input: syntax, semantics, anomaly, trust, novelty, urgency, complexity, domain, sentiment, confidence, consistency, temporal pattern, spatial pattern, resource cost, risk, opportunity. Each outputs categorical (high/medium/low). Hidden channels = metadata (provenance, timing, correlation). Integrates with InputValidator (multi-dimensional validation), DecisionRouter (richer routing signal), CuriosityDrive (novelty on any of 16 channels), ThreatDetector (multi-channel threat profiling), WorkingMemory (16D signatures per item). Novel: perception beyond the visible.
